hello_robot.py.title: Hello robot (message and green light)
hello_robot.py.summary: Shows a short message on the robot's screen and turns the light ring green for 5 seconds. The easiest way to check that your program can talk to the robot.

examples.what: shows the message and a green ring for 5 seconds

hello_robot.py.stop: Ends by itself after 5 seconds. The ring goes back to the robot's own pattern at the end.
notes: The message text and the time are constants (MESSAGE, SECONDS) at the top of the file; edit them in the Code tab.
Ctrl+C during the 5 seconds may leave the ring green until another program changes it [to verify].

scan_test.py.title: Nearest object (lidar)
scan_test.py.summary: Prints the distance to the nearest thing the lidar sees, again and again. Walk up to the robot and watch the number change.

examples.what: prints 'Nearest object: 1.23 m' for every scan

scan_test.py.stop: Runs until you stop it: Ctrl+C, or the Stop button in Studio.
notes: The lidar is switched off while the robot is on the dock, so nothing is printed there.

clearance_check.py.title: Is the way ahead clear? (one lidar scan)
clearance_check.py.summary: Takes one lidar scan and reports the nearest object within 30 degrees of straight ahead. The exit code tells scripts the answer: 0 clear, 1 blocked, 2 no scan.

args.name: min_metres
args.help: optional: the distance that counts as clear, in metres (default 0.6)

examples.what: checks for 0.6 m of free space ahead
checks for 0.8 m of free space ahead

clearance_check.py.stop: Finishes by itself after one scan (waits up to 40 s for a scan).
notes: Reads the lidar mounting angle (+90 degrees) from the robot's TF table; the lidar is off while docked.

drive_test.py.title: Drive forward 20 cm (simplest motion)
drive_test.py.summary: Drives straight ahead at 0.1 m/s for 2 seconds (about 20 cm) and stops. The smallest possible motion program; it has no obstacle check.

examples.what: drives about 20 cm forward and stops

drive_test.py.stop: Ends by itself after 2 seconds. Ctrl+C or the Stop button sends zero velocity; the E-STOP always works.
notes: Does not check for obstacles, the dock, ~/STOP or stale odometry. Keep 1 m clear ahead and stay next to the robot.
Speed and time are constants (SPEED, DRIVE_TIME) at the top of the file.

motion_test.sh.title: Full movement test (undock, drive, spin, dock)
motion_test.sh.summary: Undocks the robot, checks that the way ahead is clear, drives 20 cm if it is, spins once on the spot and docks again. A whole demo in one command.

examples.what: runs the whole test (start it on the dock)

motion_test.sh.stop: Ctrl+C in its terminal, or the E-STOP button. It uses the robot's built-in undock, rotate and dock actions, which do not look at the ~/STOP file [to verify].
notes: Run it as 'bash motion_test.sh'. It starts on the dock and takes a few minutes.
Docking only works if the robot can see the dock.

motion_shapes.py.title: Drive shapes (square, triangle, rotate, back and forth, figure eight)
motion_shapes.py.summary: Drives a shape on the floor using the wheel odometry, with obstacle, bump, stall and timeout stops. Always do a dry run first.

args.name: shape
args.help: square, triangle, rotate, back_and_forth or figure_eight

args.name: --side
args.help: side or leg length in metres (default 0.40, max 1.0)

args.name: --speed
args.help: forward speed in m/s (default 0.10, capped at 0.15)

args.name: --turn-speed
args.help: turn speed in rad/s (default 0.5, capped at 1.0)

args.name: --no-lidar
args.help: do not use the lidar: NO obstacle stop (only if the lidar is broken)

args.name: --dry-run
args.help: run the checks and print the plan, never move

args.name: --yes
args.help: skip the 'area clear?' question (needed when run from Studio)

examples.what: checks everything and prints the plan, never moves
drives a 30 cm square
one full turn on the spot

motion_shapes.py.stop: Ctrl+C, the Stop button, the E-STOP, 'touch ~/STOP', or kill -INT. It also stops itself on a bump, an obstacle closer than 0.25 m ahead, stale odometry or lidar, a stall or a timeout.
notes: Needs about 1 m of clear floor all round.
It refuses to start while the robot is docked.
Exit codes: 0 done, 1 safety stop, 2 setup failure, 130 stopped by you.

more_shapes.py.title: More shapes (polygon, star, circle, spiral, zigzag, repeatability)
more_shapes.py.summary: Builds on motion_shapes.py: drives a polygon, a star, a circle, a square spiral or a zigzag, or repeats a shape several times and reports the odometry error of each loop.

args.name: shape
args.help: polygon, star, circle, square_spiral, zigzag or repeatability

args.name: --sides
args.help: polygon: number of sides (3 to 12, default 5)

args.name: --side
args.help: side or leg length in metres (default 0.30, zigzag 0.25, max 0.60)

args.name: --radius
args.help: circle radius in metres (0.15 to 0.45, default 0.25)

args.name: --step
args.help: square_spiral: how much each leg grows, in metres (default 0.10)

args.name: --max-leg
args.help: square_spiral: longest leg in metres (default 0.50, at most 0.5)

args.name: --legs
args.help: zigzag: number of legs (1 to 8, default 4)

args.name: --shape
args.help: repeatability: which closed shape to repeat (default square)

args.name: --loops
args.help: repeatability: how many times (1 to 5, default 3)

args.name: --speed
args.help: forward speed in m/s (default 0.10, capped at 0.15)

args.name: --turn-speed
args.help: turn speed in rad/s (default 0.5, capped at 1.0)

args.name: --no-lidar
args.help: do not use the lidar: NO obstacle stop

args.name: --dry-run
args.help: run the checks and print the plan, never move

args.name: --yes
args.help: skip the 'area clear?' question (needed when run from Studio)

examples.what: checks everything and prints the star plan
drives a hexagon with 25 cm sides
drives one full circle

more_shapes.py.stop: Same as motion_shapes.py: Ctrl+C, the Stop button, the E-STOP, 'touch ~/STOP'. It also aborts if odometry puts the robot more than 1.2 m from its start, or after its total timeout.
notes: Needs motion_shapes.py and motion_common.py in the same folder on the robot.
The README says 'not yet tested on the robot' for this program.
The default --side here is 0.30 m (in the code); motion_shapes.py uses 0.40 m.

wall_approach.py.title: Approach a wall to a set distance
wall_approach.py.summary: Drives slowly towards a wall or a big flat box until the lidar reads the target distance, then compares what the wheels measured with what the lidar measured.

args.name: --target
args.help: stop distance to the wall in metres (default 0.50, min 0.30, max 2.0)

args.name: --max-travel
args.help: most it may drive in metres (at most 1.0)

args.name: --speed
args.help: forward speed in m/s (default 0.08, capped at 0.15)

args.name: --csv
args.help: write the measured samples to this CSV file

args.name: --dry-run
args.help: run the checks and show the start range, never move

args.name: --yes
args.help: skip the 'area clear?' question (needed when run from Studio)

examples.what: shows the distance to the wall and the planned travel
stops 50 cm from the wall

wall_approach.py.stop: Ctrl+C, the Stop button, the E-STOP, 'touch ~/STOP'. Also stops on a bump, stale odometry or lidar, or a timeout.
notes: Point the robot at a wall 0.5 to 1.5 m away.
Needs motion_shapes.py and motion_common.py in the same folder.
The README says 'not yet tested on the robot' for this program.

keep_distance.py.title: Keep a distance to what is in front
keep_distance.py.summary: Holds about 0.6 m to the object straight ahead: walk away and the robot follows, walk closer and it backs off slowly. Runs for at most 60 seconds.

args.name: --target
args.help: distance to hold in metres (default 0.60, 0.40 to 1.0)

args.name: --duration
args.help: run time in seconds (default and maximum 60)

args.name: --speed
args.help: maximum forward speed in m/s (default 0.10, capped at 0.15)

args.name: --dry-run
args.help: run the checks only, never move

args.name: --yes
args.help: skip the 'area clear?' question (needed when run from Studio)

examples.what: checks the sensors, never moves
follows you for 30 seconds

keep_distance.py.stop: Ends after --duration. Ctrl+C, the Stop button, the E-STOP or 'touch ~/STOP' stop it at once.
notes: Backs up at most 0.2 m and only at 0.05 m/s, because nothing watches behind the robot.
Needs motion_shapes.py and motion_common.py in the same folder.
The README says 'not yet tested on the robot' for this program.

campaign.sh.title: Run several shape programs in a row
campaign.sh.summary: Runs a list of motion_shapes.py / more_shapes.py commands one after another, with a sensor report before and after, and writes everything to a log file. Stops at the first failure.

args.name: list_file
args.help: optional: a text file with one command per line, e.g. 'more_shapes.py star --side 0.3' (default: a built-in list of six shapes)

args.name: --dry-run
args.help: run every command as a dry run, nothing moves

examples.what: runs the built-in list as dry runs

campaign.sh.stop: 'touch ~/STOP' (the running program stops the robot and the campaign ends), or kill -TERM on campaign.sh. Run from Studio, the Stop button does this for you.
notes: Run it as 'bash campaign.sh'. Every command gets --yes added, so starting it confirms the safety checklist.
Logs go to ~/robot_code/logs/.
The README says 'not yet tested on the robot' for this program.

sensor_report.py.title: Sensor report (rates, gaps, battery)
sensor_report.py.summary: Listens for 20 seconds and prints, for each sensor topic, how many messages arrived, how often, and the longest gap. The tool to use when the odometry pauses.

args.name: --seconds
args.help: measuring time in seconds (default 20)

args.name: --json
args.help: also write the report to this JSON file

examples.what: 20-second report
60-second report saved as JSON

sensor_report.py.stop: Ends after --seconds. Ctrl+C ends it early and still prints the report for the time measured.
notes: On the dock /scan shows 0 messages: the lidar is off there, which is normal.
Exit code 2 means no messages at all.
The README says 'not yet tested on the robot' for this program.

lidar_snapshot.py.title: Save a lidar scan to a file
lidar_snapshot.py.summary: Saves one or more lidar scans to a JSON or CSV file (angles in the robot's own frame) and prints the nearest return in each of 36 sectors around the robot.

args.name: --count
args.help: number of scans to save (default 1)

args.name: --out
args.help: output file, .json or .csv (default ~/robot_code/scan_<date>_<time>.json)

examples.what: saves one scan
saves five scans to room.json

lidar_snapshot.py.stop: Finishes by itself after the scans are saved (waits up to 30 s). Ctrl+C stops it early.
notes: Exit code 2 means no scan (docked? lidar off?).
Turn the JSON into a picture with scan_plot_html.py.
The README says 'not yet tested on the robot' for this program.

scan_plot_html.py.title: Draw a saved lidar scan as a picture
scan_plot_html.py.summary: Turns a lidar_snapshot.py JSON file into an HTML page with a polar plot: the robot is in the middle, forward is up. Needs no ROS, so it also runs on your own computer.

args.name: json_file
args.help: the JSON file written by lidar_snapshot.py

args.name: --out
args.help: output HTML file (default: the JSON name with .html)

args.name: --max-range
args.help: plot range in metres (default: automatic)

examples.what: writes room.html next to the JSON file
zooms to 3 m

notes: Exit code 2 means a bad input file.
Open the HTML file in any browser.

lightring_status.py.title: Show the battery and lidar state on the light ring
lightring_status.py.summary: Uses the six LEDs of the light ring as a status display: the number of lit LEDs is the battery level, the colour says how healthy it is, and blinking red means the lidar went silent.

args.name: --seconds
args.help: run time in seconds (default 30, maximum 600)

examples.what: shows the state for 30 seconds
shows it for two minutes

lightring_status.py.stop: Ends after --seconds, or on Ctrl+C / SIGTERM. It always hands the ring back to the robot at the end.
notes: Green is 50 % battery or more, yellow 20 to 50 %, red below 20 %.

health_check.py.title: Robot health checklist
health_check.py.summary: Checks Wi-Fi, the ROS service, the base data and battery, the clocks, the lidar, odometry gaps, temperature, memory and more, and prints one PASS / WARN / FAIL row each with a hint how to fix it. Read only.

args.name: --seconds
args.help: ROS measuring window in seconds (default 10, maximum 120)

args.name: --json
args.help: also write the report to this JSON file

examples.what: the normal check (15 to 25 seconds)
a longer check, saved as JSON

health_check.py.stop: Ends by itself (about 15 to 25 s, 45 s when the base is silent). Ctrl+C stops it.
notes: Never moves the robot, changes nothing and needs no sudo.
Exit code 0 all PASS or INFO, 1 at least one WARN, 2 at least one FAIL.
The README says 'not yet tested on the robot' for this program.

motion_common.py.title: Shared safety code (not a program)
motion_common.py.summary: A helper module used by more_shapes.py, wall_approach.py and keep_distance.py: start-up checks, total timeout and a 1.2 m fence. It is not run directly; keep it next to those programs.
notes: Copy it to the robot together with motion_shapes.py and the programs that use it.

my_first_program.py.title: Template: my first program (read the robot)
my_first_program.py.summary: The hello world of robot code. Prints the battery, whether the robot is on the dock and where it is, once a second for 10 seconds. Heavily commented: start here to learn how ROS 2 programs work.

examples.what: prints a status line every second for 10 seconds

my_first_program.py.stop: Ends by itself after 10 seconds, or on Ctrl+C.
notes: Copy it with 'New program' in the Code tab and change it. Change SECONDS first.

read_lidar.py.title: Template: read the lidar
read_lidar.py.summary: Prints the nearest thing ahead, left, right and behind the robot once a second for 20 seconds, and explains why the lidar's angles are turned by 90 degrees on this robot.

examples.what: prints the four distances every second for 20 seconds

read_lidar.py.stop: Ends by itself after 20 seconds, or on Ctrl+C.
notes: The lidar is off while the robot is docked: you will see 'no scan yet'. Undock first.
Change SECONDS or HALF_ANGLE first.

spin_in_place.py.title: Template: spin on the spot
spin_in_place.py.summary: Turns the robot in place for the number of turns you ask for and stops exactly, counting the angle from the odometry. The answer to 'make it spin around'.

args.name: --turns
args.help: full turns, negative = turn right (default 1, max 5)

args.name: --speed
args.help: turn speed in rad/s (default 0.5, capped at 1.0)

args.name: --dry-run
args.help: check the robot and print the plan, never move

args.name: --yes
args.help: skip the 'area clear?' question (needed when run from Studio)

examples.what: checks the robot, never moves
one full turn to the left
two turns to the right, faster

spin_in_place.py.stop: Ctrl+C, the Stop button, the E-STOP, 'touch ~/STOP', stale odometry, a bump, or the 90 s time limit. Zero velocity is sent on every way out.
notes: Refuses to start while the robot is docked: undock first.
Change TURNS and SPEED first.

drive_circle.py.title: Template: drive in a circle
drive_circle.py.summary: Drives a circle of the radius you choose and stops where it started. It sends a forward speed and a turn rate together (turn rate = speed / radius) and counts the laps from the odometry heading.

args.name: --radius
args.help: circle radius in metres (default 0.30, 0.15 to 0.5)

args.name: --speed
args.help: forward speed in m/s (default 0.10, capped at 0.15)

args.name: --laps
args.help: number of laps, negative = circle to the right (default 1, max 3)

args.name: --dry-run
args.help: check the robot and print the plan, never move

args.name: --yes
args.help: skip the 'area clear?' question (needed when run from Studio)

examples.what: checks the robot, never moves
one lap of a 30 cm radius circle

drive_circle.py.stop: Ctrl+C, the Stop button, the E-STOP, 'touch ~/STOP', an obstacle closer than 0.35 m ahead, stale odometry or lidar, a bump, or the 90 s time limit. Zero velocity is sent on every way out.
notes: Needs about 1 m of clear floor all round.
Change RADIUS and SPEED first.

drive_forward_and_back.py.title: Template: drive forward and come back
drive_forward_and_back.py.summary: Drives forward a set distance, turns round, drives back to the start and turns to face forward again, measuring the distance with the odometry and watching the lidar for obstacles.

args.name: --distance
args.help: metres to drive out (default 0.30, max 1.0)

args.name: --speed
args.help: forward speed in m/s (default 0.10, capped at 0.15)

args.name: --dry-run
args.help: check the robot and print the plan, never move

args.name: --yes
args.help: skip the 'area clear?' question (needed when run from Studio)

examples.what: checks the robot, never moves
30 cm out and 30 cm back

drive_forward_and_back.py.stop: Ctrl+C, the Stop button, the E-STOP, 'touch ~/STOP', an obstacle closer than 0.35 m ahead, stale odometry or lidar, a bump, or the 90 s time limit. Zero velocity is sent on every way out.
notes: It never reverses (the Create 3 limits backing up): it turns round instead.
Change DISTANCE and SPEED first.
